title: FBI: Fingerprint submission, Portland Police Bureau case 94-99422 / Multnomah County ME case 94-2962 (Oct. 1994)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, I request the following records:

1. Any fingerprint submission received from the Portland Police Bureau, the Multnomah County Medical Examiner's Office, or the Oregon State Police between October 18, 1994 and December 31, 1994 concerning an unidentified deceased white female found in a Portland, Oregon motel on or about October 18, 1994 (PPB case no. 94-99422; Multnomah County ME case no. 94-2962).

2. Any response, search result, "non-identification" notice, or correspondence returned to the submitting agency about that submission.

3. Any later search, comparison, or retention of those prints, including in the unidentified person or unknown deceased files.

4. If no submission was received, a statement to that effect.

This request rests on the Multnomah County Medical Examiner's follow-up report, entry of 10/20/94, 09:03 hrs, which states Portland Police ID ran the prints locally and through AFIS and "will forward the prints to the FBI." I do not know whether the submission was made. The decedent has never been identified, and no named individual is the subject of this request.

For context, this case has long been discussed online: 

https://websleuths.com/threads/or-portland-whtfem-35-55-up9936-suicide-hotel-surgical-scars-lft-knee-rt-breast-dec94.165575/

https://unidentified-awareness.fandom.com/wiki/Multnomah_County_Jane_Doe_(1994)

https://www.reddit.com/r/UnresolvedMysteries/comments/8znefv/in_1994_a_woman_was_found_dead_after_having/

Thank you for the work that the bureau does each and every day, and thank you for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
